title: 1963 AHSME Problem 20
statement: Two men at points \(R\) and \(S,\) \(76\) miles apart, set out at the same time to walk towards each other. The man at \(R\) walks uniformly at \(4\dfrac12\) miles per hour; the man at \(S\) walks at \(3\dfrac14\) miles per hour for the first hour, at \(3\dfrac34\) miles per hour for the second hour, and so on, in arithmetic progression. If the men meet \(x\) miles nearer \(R\) than \(S\) in an integral number of hours, then \(x\) is:

solutions.text:
In \(h\) hours the first man walks \(\frac{9h}{2}.\) The second walks an arithmetic-series total \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac h2\left(2\cdot\frac{13}{4} +(h-1)\frac12\right)\\ &\qquad=3h+\frac{h^2}{4}. \end{aligned} \] Their distances sum to \(76,\) giving \(h^2+30h-304=0,\) whose positive root is \(h=8.\) They walk \(36\) and \(40\) miles, so the meeting point is \(4\) miles nearer \(R\) than \(S.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the integral meeting time be \(h\) hours and sum the second man’s hourly distances
